audit_findings.title: Ch5 Definition 5.3.1 Stage-1 non-work-conserving overwrite, unreachable 0.85/0.15 scoring branch, and duplicate context feature channel
audit_findings.manuscript_claim: Two-stage release-time work-conserving approximation eliminating unready tasks blocking ready tasks; 0.85/0.15 split when min(3.0, s_n) < tau_done <= s_n; 14-D public context vector
audit_findings.repo_value: Stage 1 iterates in static (deadline, uid) order and overwrites t_bh_free/t_inter_free = t_tr_done (non-work-conserving when earlier-deadline task has longer uplink than ready task, and single-channel vs Engine._rates equal bandwidth sharing across active directed links); relative deadlines D_n in [2.0, 3.0] s imply s_n <= 3.0 s for all existing tasks so min(3.0, s_n) == s_n and the 0.85/0.15 branch is unreachable; context[3] and context[9] are identical (win3 / 60.0)

audit_findings.title: Ch3 symmetric DSR decomposition unit-level vs macro-mean aggregation & undocumented 100-UE penalized system latency denominator
audit_findings.manuscript_claim: Symmetric decomposition gives +4.87 pp admission and -2.02 pp post-admission quality (+2.85 pp net); penalized system latency per generated service request drops from 33.73 s to 28.15 s
audit_findings.repo_value: Averaging symmetric decomposition across the 50 units yields +4.8664 pp and -2.0155 pp (sum +2.8509 pp, matching prose +4.87 / -2.02 / +2.85 pp), whereas plugging Table 3-5 macro means into Eq. (2-16) gives +4.8877 pp and -2.0237 pp (sum +2.8641 pp != +2.8509 pp due to multi-episode covariance inside each unit). Penalized latency sums 20.0 s penalty across ALL 100 UEs without a timely completion (including idle UEs and content-request UEs) and divides that 100-UE sum by ~33.8 generated service requests, producing values > 20.0 s (33.73 s and 28.15 s)
